lines.text: What would you love to buy one day? Today you will make a real plan to get there, one week at a time.
A goal is something you want to buy later, like a cycle or a cricket bat.
A clear goal has a name, a price and a date.
For example, a ₹900 cricket bat by the summer holidays is a clear goal.
Divide the price by the amount you can save each week.
A ₹900 bat with ₹100 saved each week takes 9 weeks.
Save a little more each week, and you get there sooner.
Draw a savings chart and colour one box every time you add money.
Watching the chart fill up keeps you going.
Write the date next to each box.
Saving takes patience, like waiting for a mango to ripen.
Every time you skip a small want, your goal comes closer.
If you miss a week, simply start again the next week.
Birthday money, festival gifts or money for helping at home are boosts.
Put part of every boost into your goal.
You will be surprised how fast it grows.
Meera wants a cycle that costs three thousand rupees, and she wants it by Diwali.
She already has six hundred rupees saved, so she needs two thousand four hundred rupees more.
She can save two hundred rupees every week from her pocket money and helping at home.
Two thousand four hundred divided by two hundred is twelve, so Meera needs twelve weeks.
Kabir is saving one hundred rupees a week for a nine hundred rupee cricket bat.
He colours one box on his chart every week, so he can see his savings grow.
In week three he spent his money on snacks, so he did not colour a box.
He did not give up, and in week ten his chart was full and he bought the bat.
Riya sees a lollipop for twenty rupees, and she really wants it.
She is also saving for a board game that costs four hundred and eighty rupees.
She thinks about her goal, puts the twenty rupees in her Save jar, and colours her chart.
Choosing later over now is hard, and that is exactly what makes saving a superpower.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
